scope: Every unexplained_generated_symbol finding recorded in logs/failed-solves at audit time.

classifications.representativePattern: t=\arctan x and x=\tan t in the substitution step
classifications.rationale: The change of variable explicitly introduces t, but the historical validator did not propagate all rendered introduction fields.

classifications.representativePattern: an inner-integral identity uses n in a later step after n was only a local sum index
classifications.rationale: The candidate does not declare n as a persistent parameter before the standalone identity.

classifications.representativePattern: x=\tan\theta in the first substitution step
classifications.rationale: Theta is explicitly introduced by the change of variable and used afterward.

classifications.representativePattern: integration-by-parts steps use n after its local summation scope
classifications.rationale: The derivation needs an explicit for-each-n parameter declaration; a prior sum binder must not leak.

classifications.representativePattern: B_{2n} is described in prose as Bernoulli numbers but is not formally defined
classifications.rationale: A reader can identify the standard sequence, but accepting every prose name would hide undefined coefficient families.

classifications.representativePattern: B_{2n} appears in a split line and inline summary whose containing full equation has sum_{n=1}
classifications.rationale: The full step binds n; only presentation slices lost the operator context.
The prose/math declaration explicitly names the constant before the final answer.
The named-constant phrase explicitly identifies G in the same step.
